entry.title: A green pipeline that deployed nothing
entry.summary:
The worst CI outcome is not a failing build. It is a passing build that did Here is one way to get there, and it takes a single missing line of YAML. A pipeline that deploys only what changed. It diffs against the parent commit, files = run_git(["diff", "--name-only", base, head], repo_root)
Azure DevOps can check out with shallow fetch. A shallow clone has no parent So git diff HEAD~1 HEAD does not error. It returns nothing. Nothing changed, therefore nothing needs deploying, therefore every stage skips, You find out later, when something that was supposed to be in production is not. Make the pipeline correct: - checkout: self fetchDepth: 0
And make the script refuse to guess: if run_git(["rev-parse", "--is-shallow-repository"], repo_root) == "true": raise GitError( "This is a shallow clone, so there is no history to diff against.\n" "Set 'fetchDepth: 0' on the checkout step, or disable shallow fetch " "in the pipeline settings." )
The second part matters more than the first. fetchDepth: 0 is one line in a def test_detection_stage_checks_out_full_history(self): checkout = detect_stage["jobs"][0]["steps"][0] self.assertEqual(checkout.get("checkout"), "self") self.assertEqual( checkout.get("fetchDepth"), 0, "change detection needs full history; fetchDepth must be 0", )
It parses the pipeline YAML and asserts the line is still there. Slightly Ask of any conditional deployment: what does this do when its input is
Wrong input usually errors. Missing input often produces an empty result that Anywhere those two are indistinguishable, make the code refuse rather than Full context: [https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/enterprise-microsoft-fabric-cicd-selective-one-azure-devops-ghosh-uxzsf] https://github.com/VEDAFORGE/fabric-cicd-reference/tree/v2.0.0]
